label: Только
description: A 10-sentence usage card for только (only, just), a restrictive focus adverb.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Restricting the object. 'Только' means only and restricts focus to the word right after it, here 'хлеб'. Placed before the object, it says bread and nothing else was bought.
Strategic focus: Restricting the subject. Moving 'только' before 'я' shifts the focus to the subject, meaning only I and no one else know the truth. Placement controls what is singled out.
Strategic focus: Restricting time. 'Только' before 'по утрам' limits the focus to the mornings, meaning he works at no other time. The adverb narrows attention to the phrase it precedes.
Strategic focus: Softening with just. 'Только' before 'хотел' means just or merely, softening the verb to I only wanted to help. Here it downplays the intent rather than counting items.
Strategic focus: Restricting a limit. 'Только' before 'до шести' marks only until six, stressing the cutoff. The adverb focuses on the time phrase to highlight the boundary.
Strategic focus: Только что for just now. The fixed phrase 'только что' means a moment ago, marking a very recent action. This temporal idiom differs from the restrictive only.
Strategic focus: Restricting quantity. 'Только' before 'один' limits the focus to a single ticket, meaning just one and no more. The adverb tightens the count it precedes.
Strategic focus: Restricting the focus of thought. 'Только' before 'о себе' means thinks only about herself. The adverb narrows attention to that phrase and carries a critical tone.
Strategic focus: Как только as as soon as. The phrase 'как только' is a conjunction meaning as soon as, linking the arrival to becoming free. This connective use differs from the restrictive only.
Strategic focus: Only as merely. 'Только' before 'начало' means this is just the beginning, restricting the noun to a mere starting point. The adverb minimises what follows.
